mcat_description.short: GI Portable Cabin is a prefabricated, relocatable structure with a galvanised iron sheet exterior and mild steel frame, sold as a complete unit for use as a security cabin, site office, temporary shop, or labour accommodation.
mcat_description.long: A GI (Galvanised Iron) Portable Cabin is a factory-built prefabricated structure constructed using a mild steel tubular or C-channel base frame with GI corrugated sheet cladding on exterior walls and roof, typically 1.0–1.2 mm thick, with internal wall panelling of pre-laminated MDF or bison board and 18 mm MR-grade plywood flooring. Cabins are supplied with glass wool or thermacool insulation, aluminium powder-coated sliding windows, an MS door, concealed ISI-grade copper wiring, and epoxy primer plus enamel paint finish. Standard sizes range from compact 6×4 ft security booths to large 10×40 ft site offices, with custom dimensions available; the modular design allows stacking, linking, and relocation by crane or truck. In the Indian market, GI portable cabins are the cost-effective alternative to permanent construction for construction sites, industrial facilities, toll booths, event venues, and remote project locations.

market_context: GI Portable Cabins in India are prefabricated structures with a galvanised iron sheet exterior (typically 1.0–1.2 mm thick GI corrugated sheet) over a mild steel C-channel or tubular frame, factory-assembled and delivered as complete units. The Indian market distinguishes GI cabins from PUF panel cabins, sandwich panel cabins, FRP cabins, and MS cabins by the material of the exterior cladding — 'GI' specifically signals galvanised iron sheet construction. Key manufacturing hubs include Thane/Navi Mumbai (Maharashtra), Ahmedabad (Gujarat), Delhi/NCR, and Pune. Buyers evaluate primarily on GI sheet thickness, frame section size, insulation type (glass wool vs thermacool vs PUF), dimensions, and finish quality (epoxy vs enamel paint). Standard structural specifications include a 100×50 mm C-channel bottom frame, 75×40 mm stiffener, 1.2 mm GI roof sheet, 8 mm pre-laminated MDF internal panelling, and 18 mm MR-grade plywood flooring — this specification is consistent across multiple independent manufacturers. IS-grade materials are referenced by manufacturers (IS-marked GI sheet, ISI-marked wiring), though no single BIS product standard exclusively governs the assembled cabin. Security cabin and site office are the two dominant commercial sub-types by volume; the 'gomti/gumti' small shop cabin is a distinct sub-segment driven by roadside vendor demand (confirmed by Hindi keyword data). Rental and sale are both common transaction modes for construction site use.
